clue.text: Angler beginning to fill one kind of tank

indicators.note: the beginning of the word fill supplies just its opening letter here

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the Sherman was an American tank of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Someone who fishes starts stocking a particular type of aquarium.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes angling with rod and line is a fisher of the sport.

clue.text: Haughty fellow rings to be admitted

indicators.note: the rings are let inside the fellow, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, standing for any fellow
two rings look like the letters O and O

explanation.surface: A stuck-up man wears rings to get into somewhere exclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone distant and superior, keeping others at arm's length.

clue.text: Sea creature prince smuggled back west initially

indicators.note: back tells us the word for smuggled is written right to left

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of west

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A marine animal, with a prince, is secretly brought back westward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusked Arctic whale, so certainly a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Bone found in Indian city?

parts.note: Patel is a very common Indian surname, so an Indian person may be a Patel
LA is Los Angeles, the city

explanation.surface: A bone is discovered somewhere in a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian city' reads as one place, but splits into an Indian (Patel, a common surname) and a city (LA); the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the small bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: At Bethnal Green, go underground and carp

indicators.note: Bethnal Green is in London's East End, where Cockney speakers drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: to go underground is to hide away

explanation.surface: In an East London district, people go into hiding and complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like a verb meaning complain; it is the fish. Bethnal Green is a Cockney area of East London, and Cockneys famously drop initial Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the orfe.

clue.text: Land with husky, say, and animal for riding

parts.note: to land someone with a burden is to saddle them with it

indicators.note: say signals that we want a word that is pronounced like hoarse

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: Somebody gets stuck with a sled dog as well as a mount to ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' suggests the sled dog, but it means hoarse-voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse kept and trained for being ridden rather than pulling carts.

clue.text: Routed all over the place, following this?

definitions.text: Routed all over the place, following this?

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone driving a diversion finds they are sent everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion from the usual road sends drivers by a roundabout route.

clue.text: Roman family name of Swiss financier involved in scam

indicators.note: the financier is placed inside the scam, wrapped up in it

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
the gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker's family name turns up in a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The gnomes of Zurich is a jibe at Swiss bankers, so a gnome is a Swiss financier.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the third name, shared by a branch of a clan, such as Caesar.

clue.text: Given illumination, landed with provisions around lake

indicators.note: around says the provisions go about the lake

parts.note: provisions are food supplies
a bird that has landed has lit on something

explanation.surface: A lit-up arrival comes ashore with supplies near the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit by strong lamps, as a stadium is at night under bright lights.

clue.text: Watchman with energy replacing a form of fuel

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a patrol is a watchman going round
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A security guard full of energy substitutes for a type of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuel that cars run on, called gasoline in the US.

clue.text: Gap in continuity true men grin about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine chaps smile around a break in proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between two reigns or regimes, when rule is interrupted.

clue.text: A bad name for earthy particles mixed with water?

definitions.meaning: someone in disgrace is said to have their name as this
soil and water mixed make a wet sticky substance

explanation.surface: A rude label for dirty slurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet earth, and also a word for a disgraced name in the idiom.

clue.text: Ban doctor interrupting organ work?

indicators.note: the doctor breaks into the organ, sitting inside it

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine qualification
go means to work or function

explanation.surface: A physician stops a church organist from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument; it is a body part, the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Ill-educated youth leader lacking preparedness

parts.note: someone unread has not read much, so is ill-educated

indicators.note: the leader of youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: An uncultured youth leader is not prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Not prepared or ready for action, as the nickname of King Ethelred.

clue.text: Rubbish put back thus in trunk

indicators.note: put back means the word for rubbish is turned round

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Garbage is put back into a storage chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: English composer's seen around principal part of fortifications

indicators.note: the composer is seen around the letter for English, enclosing it

parts.note: Bach is the German composer; the 's is read as is
a head is a principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: An English composer is spotted near the main part of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A defended position on a shore won by landing troops, part of a military defence.

clue.text: Amusing chap reportedly supplying mushrooms and the like

indicators.note: reportedly means we take what the clue phrase sounds like when spoken

parts.note: an amusing chap is a fun guy

explanation.surface: A funny man is said to supply mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the group including mushrooms, toadstools and moulds.

clue.text: Poisonous type exhausted crossing eastern river

indicators.note: crossing means the exhausted word spans the other letters, holding them

parts.note: spent means used up, exhausted

explanation.surface: A venomous man, worn out, goes over an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake, some of which are venomous; also a treacherous person.

clue.text: Depth measurer that's safer under City house?

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts safer below the City house letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
sounder means more secure, safer

explanation.surface: A depth gauge is more secure below a City house.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonar device that measures sea depth by timing reflected sound pulses.

clue.text: Air of this writer accepting rise in benefit?

indicators.note: accepting means the writer's word takes the other inside it

parts.note: this writer stands for the setter, whose possessive is my

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Is my manner raised by an increase in welfare payments?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like atmosphere but is a tune. The dole is the British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, a sequence of notes.

clue.text: Emperor who's down over Christmas rising

parts.note: nap is the downy pile on fabric
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

explanation.surface: A ruler feels low over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' seems to mean sad but is the soft pile called nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was Emperor of the French.

clue.text: Small island with a special appeal

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, the special something

explanation.surface: An island with particular charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot, a small island in a river such as the Thames.

clue.text: One in stagnation, with no tips on where to find fuel?

indicators.note: in places one inside the trimmed word
no tips means the end letters of the word are cut

parts.note: the doldrums are a state of stagnation
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a rut gets no hints on where fuel is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tips' strips D and S from DOLDRUMS, leaving OLDRUM, into which 'in' puts I.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel for oil, a place where fuel is kept; the question mark marks the loose definition.

clue.text: Left Arran sadly, like close relatives

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone departed a Scottish island in sorrow, as family do.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Brotherly, as close kin are to each other.

clue.text: Suspicion surrounding most of European Right's protest

indicators.note: surrounding means the suspicion encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a hunch is a suspicion

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a German is a European
R is the abbreviation for right; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A suspicion hangs over a European right-wing demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration march by the unemployed, as in 1930s Britain.

clue.text: Shy — not like us when given papers for Queen

indicators.note: when given signals that the word receives something new in exchange
for means in place of, so papers stand where Queen stood

parts.note: different means not like us
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
ID is identification papers

explanation.surface: A timid person, unlike us, is given documents in place of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking confidence, bashful.

clue.text: Explosive device — what mine host might call a failure?

parts.note: mine host is a pub landlord, who calls time at closing
a show that bombs is a failure

explanation.surface: A bomb with a pub landlord calling it a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine host' is a jocular term for a pub landlord, who calls 'Time!' at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb set to explode at a set moment.

clue.text: Month cook loses head, eating beef regularly

indicators.note: eating means the trimmed word takes the other letters inside it
loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to doctor figures is to cook them, falsify

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of beef

explanation.surface: A cook beheaded eating beef regularly in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a chef but is the verb doctor; 'loses head' gives OCTOR, and 'regularly' gives BE from beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the year.

clue.text: Odd time to bury minute items of jumble

indicators.note: to bury means the other pieces enclose minute

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A strange time to bury tiny bits of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: A rummage sale is a jumble sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummage is goods for a rummage sale, odds and ends.

clue.text: Hoof extremely useful in a wildebeest when climbing

indicators.note: in places the extremes inside the climbing word
in a down clue climbing means the words are written upwards

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of useful

explanation.surface: Hooves are very handy for a wildebeest climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoof or claw in zoology.

clue.text: Spirit of nature in lines framed by old man

indicators.note: framed by means the old man surrounds the lines

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A nature spirit is kept within lines by an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood nymph in Greek mythology.

clue.text: After end of dinner, I love a port

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of dinner

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: After dinner, I love a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport.
